message.content:
I see - the fuzzer uses `ib = hoedown_buffer_new(opt.iunit)` where `opt.iunit = DEF_IUNIT = 1024`. So `ib` is a buffer with unit=1024. Then `hoedown_buffer_put(ib, data, size)` copies the input data into `ib`. The `ib->size` is set to `size`, and `ib->asize` is at least 1024 (rounded up from `size`).

Then `hoedown_document_render(document, ob, ib->data, ib->size)` is called. Inside, `text = hoedown_buffer_new(64)` and `hoedown_buffer_grow(text, ib->size)` grows `text` to at least `ib->size` bytes (in multiples of 64).

So the `text` buffer has `asize >= ib->size` (rounded up to multiple of 64). The OOB read at `text->data[3]` when `size = 3` is within the buffer.

I think the key insight I'm missing is that the vulnerability might be detected by a different mechanism. Let me look at the submission script:
